content: {"rules": ["Model forecasts tend to overestimate prices in early cycles and show mean-reversion bias as prices drop sharply after peak forecasts.", "Sentiment spikes (especially above 0.67) correlate with forecast overshoots, suggesting sentiment drives short-term price volatility.", "Forecast accuracy declines when sentiment is mixed or negative, indicating sentiment interaction weakens predictive power.", "Model forecasts often lag actual price movements, particularly in downward trends, suggesting delayed reaction to market signals.", "High sentiment positivity (1.00) is associated with forecast overestimation, especially in the first 10 days of the forecast window.", "Forecast bias is more pronounced in later days of the 30-day window, indicating diminishing predictive reliability over time.", "Sentiment negativity (-1.00) consistently precedes sharp price declines, suggesting sentiment can trigger mean-reversion or reversal events."]}
